{"id": "571ca809-d929-4f52-adc3-26765188ef20", "role": "assistant", "block_type": "run_subagent", "content": [{"type": "tool_result", "tool_use_id": "tooluse_jzyis6EeCFMAMyPK6xSGMi", "status": "success", "content": [{"text": "## Root Cause Found: Private DNS is NOT enabled on the EC2 interface endpoint

Since DNS resolution isn't being overridden (private DNS off), standard EC2 API calls to `ec2.us-east-1.amazonaws.com` resolve to AWS public IPs and fall through to this default route → NAT. |

`vpce-0e4fa5a4b939c0a07` (GuardDuty) **does** have `PrivateDnsEnabled: true` and works correctly — useful as an in-account comparison confirming the EC2 endpoint's `false` setting is the anomaly, not a region/account-wide default.
